why: 2 invocations for the substitute, 0 for the kit. The kit's version is the editorial half of skill authoring — invocation choice, information hierarchy, progressive disclosure, precedent blocks, the seven failure modes. It is also 1/7th the length and user-invoked, so it has never had a chance to fire. Tests whether the editorial framing earns its place against a much larger general skill-writing guide.

evals.prompt: this skill keeps not firing when I actually need it. the description is 'Helps with data analysis tasks'. what do I do
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the description as the triggering mechanism and rewrites it with concrete trigger contexts, rather than giving generic advice about clarity.
expectations: Identifies the description field as the thing that decides invocation, not the body
Rewrites the actual description rather than describing how to rewrite it
Addresses near-miss competition — what else might claim the same queries
Explains why the original fails, not just that it does

evals.prompt: my SKILL.md is about 900 lines and two people have now told me it's too long. what do I actually cut
evals.expected_output: Applies progressive disclosure — what belongs in SKILL.md vs references/ vs scripts/ — with a concrete cut list, not a general plea for brevity.
expectations: Uses a principle for what stays vs what moves out, not just 'cut the fluff'
Names specific categories of content to relocate and where they go
Recognises that length itself is not the defect — reachability of the right content is
Gives an actionable ordering, not an undifferentiated list

evals.prompt: I keep having to give Claude the same correction every session — it writes migrations without a rollback step. I've told it like six times. how do I make it stick
evals.expected_output: Turns a recurring correction into a durable rule that survives — rule plus precedent plus self-check — rather than suggesting he just add a line to CLAUDE.md.
expectations: Produces the actual rule text, not advice about writing rules
Includes something that makes the rule verifiable or self-checking, not just a statement
Explains why bare imperatives decay and what makes one survive
Addresses where it should live so it is actually loaded when relevant
